summary.text: A 56-year-old Hispanic man with a history of chronic smoking and associated COPD has been diagnosed with lung cancer since 2012. In November 2012 CEA 6.5 ng/mL, AST 44 u/L and ALT 77 u/L were elevated, and chest CT showed calcifications of the coronary arteries and lung nodules. In March 2013 ALT was 67 u/L and CEA 13 ng/mL, both elevated.

He underwent a left lower lobe segment and tumor resection in summer 2013 and received chemotherapy with the last cycle in November 2013, including adjuvant docetaxel and carboplatin begun by week 7 and completed in week 20 post-operative. No radiation therapy was offered. High dose intravenous vitamin C started in December 2013 and continued until June 2015, with infusions of 25 gr, 50 gr and 75 gr and a maximum of 75 gr three times a week.

In August 2013 CEA improved to a level considered within normal limits, and whole-body PET/CT in November 2013 found no abnormal increased FDG uptake to suggest a hypermetabolic lesion. CEA is reported to have stayed within normal levels while high-dose vitamin C infusions were given, and the authors describe improvement during the infusions. The patient decided to stop the vitamin C treatment in June 2015 and is described as still alive and enjoying activities of daily living.
